headline: TJX beat on profit and raised EPS outlook, but T.J. Maxx/Marshalls comps slowed to 1% on self-inflicted mix errors.
guidance_note: FY27 comp held at +3-4%; FY EPS raised to $5.31-5.36 reported (incl. tariff refunds) from $5.08-5.15. Q3 comp guided +2-3%.
key_messages: Consolidated comp +4%; Marmaxx US comp only +1% (vs +3% LY), all from higher basket with a small decline in Marmaxx transactions.
HomeGoods and TJX International comps +7%, TJX Canada +6% offset the Marmaxx shortfall.
CEO Herrman called the Marmaxx miss 'self-inflicted' store-mix execution, not demand or competition; expects improvement by holiday.
Reported EPS $1.36 included a $0.14 net benefit from IEEPA tariff refunds; adjusted EPS $1.22, up 11%.
Merchandise availability 'continues to be outstanding'; TJX plans to lift store growth, citing rural markets where department stores close.

consumer.big_ticket: Home strong: HomeGoods comp +7%, while US apparel (Marmaxx) lagged on internal execution.
consumer.pricing: Quarter benefited from tariff refunds; growth at Marmaxx came from higher average basket rather than traffic.
consumer.quote: And availability of merchandise continues to be outstanding.

macro_read: Off-price demand broadly healthy, especially home, but TJX's flagship US apparel slowdown shows shoppers are selective; management blames execution, not a weaker consumer.
notes: Adjusted EPS of $1.22 already excludes a $0.14 tariff-refund benefit (reported EPS $1.36).
